svg.text: Configuring a Linux NIC (mlx5e), with the code: from ip / ethtool to the firmware
Four common setup actions, one per column. Follow a column down through the layers; every one ends in a firmware command sent through the shared path at the bottom.
built once when the driver loads
one channel per core; rings allocated in host memory
TIRs hash packets onto RQTs; flow tables pick a TIR
Rebuild the RQs, set the port MTU
RX buffers must fit the new MTU
new set first, then swap: traffic keeps flowing
open new channels, swap, close old
then DESTROY_* for the old set
the NIC posts a command EQE
the driver writes the input here; the firmware
DMA-reads it and DMA-writes the output
reads the command, checks it, creates or changes the object, then writes the output and status
What now exists in the NIC:
RQs and SQs in RDY state;
the code at that layer; indented lines are called from the line above (some steps in between are skipped)

Files: Linux drivers/net/ethernet/mellanox/mlx5/core/ (en_main.c, en_ethtool.c, en/rx_res.c, en/rqt.c, en/tir.c, transobj.c, cq.c, port.c, vport.c, fs_core.c, fs_cmd.c, cmd.c); net/core/ (rtnetlink.c, dev.c); net/ethtool/.
Checked against Linux master, November 2026. Probe and EQ setup, which run before all of this, are in Module 3 deep dive 4.2a.
